description: Groups the updates into as few PRs as possible: non-breaking ones, breaking ones and the Rust toolchain.
separateMajorMinor is off so that major updates join the breaking PR instead of getting PRs of their own.
Every version waits until it is 3 days old as a guard against supply chain attacks. Lock file maintenance stays off because Renovate cannot apply minimumReleaseAge to it.
There is no schedule and no hourly PR limit, so an update arrives as soon as it passes the cooldown.
rangeStrategy bump writes the new version into Cargo.toml too, as `cargo add` does, instead of only updating Cargo.lock.

packageRules.description: Updates that should not need code changes go into one PR.
Breaking updates go into one more PR, including minor bumps of 0.x crates, which Cargo treats as breaking.

A pin keeps the version that is already in use, so it joins the non-breaking PR without the cooldown. Renovate has no release timestamp for pins and would otherwise leave the cooldown check pending forever.
A new Rust release can add clippy lints that fail CI, so the toolchain gets its own PR.
